answer: Make each account's voting weight grow only with time spent grading strangers. A new key starts with a whisper of influence and earns more by scoring randomly drawn answers that later match the honest consensus. Sybils can wander in by the hundreds, but they arrive with velvet hands: no history, no weight. To matter they must each do months of real, checked work, and if their grades cluster too tightly the ferrous rule applies: correlated accounts share one weight, so cloning buys nothing.
